title: The tests are the check for construction and search results
body:
`CLAUDE.md` under "What must not change" says the tests are the only check that suffix array construction (the `.sufr` bytes) and search results (count, locate, extract) survive a refactor. A survey of the 110 tests on 2026-11-03 at 4e04a02 found the net thinner than the count suggests. This milestone holds the survey and the batches that fix it. Each test added, changed or removed is one commit, signed off by Jack one at a time.

## Survey

Construction, in `sufr/tests/cli.rs` unless noted:

- The four `*_is_sorted` tests (`file_is_sorted`, cli.rs:1178) are vacuous. They write the suffixes with `list -o`, which `list` ignores (sufr-974977), so the file stays empty and the loop that checks order runs zero times. They pass with a wrong sort.
- No test compares the suffix order against an independent sort. No test checks LCP values against an independent computation. The only independent LCP check is `typed.rs:795`, which compares subsamples and only sees `lcp < mql`.
- Bytes are compared only by `create_bytes_match_fixtures` (cli.rs:1273), on 13 of the 16 `data/expected/*.sufr`. The 12 `create_*` tests (cli.rs:125-301) use the same inputs and flags but compare suffix order only, through `create` (cli.rs:52), and never pass `--write-lcp`.
- `create_max_query_len` (cli.rs:1339) asserts an order identical to the unconstrained build of 1.fa, so it cannot tell `-m 3` from no `-m`. No fixture is built with `-m`, so sufr-2b76b5 (LCP above m) is pinned by nothing.
- Fixtures with no test: `data/expected/1d.sufr` (version 4, unreadable), `1m.sufr` (fails to open), `1s.sufr`, `locate2.out`; `data/inputs/empty.fa`, `3.sufr`, `abba.sufr`. `mk_test_files.py` omits `--write-lcp` (sufr-c9b319).
- Never built by a test: a delimiter other than N, an ambiguity code other than N, a record with no sequence, an empty input (`create_empty_dies` passes a path that does not exist, sufr-56f73a), an input large enough for the `rayon::join` branch in `merge_sort`. The u64 width is built once, `lib.rs:270` with `with_force_64bit`, and never searched.
- `partition`, `merge`, `merge_sort`, `sort_partition`, `first_lcps` and `find_n_run` have no unit test; only end-to-end builds reach them.

Search:

- Storage modes. The CLI helpers for locate and extract loop over none, `-l` and `-v`, so every `-m` test runs Memory+Subsampled, Memory+Disk and Disk+Disk. count has no `-m` test. The library tests pass no `max_query_len`.
- Query kinds with no test: not found and sorting before `$`, empty, containing N, containing `$` or `%`, longer than the text, equal to a whole sequence. mql equal to or longer than the query has no test.
- Extract windows with no test: `before` clamped by more than one byte, `after` past the sequence end, `after: Some(0)`. Two expectations pin the overrun of sufr-2fd179: cli.rs:561 expects `RNEEDDDG%M` and cli.rs:596 expects `RKELKKDEF%`, windows holding the delimiter and the next sequence's first residue.
- Locate order is sorted by sequence name as text then position; names that sort differently as text and numbers (`10`, `2`) have no test.
- Five `-m` CLI tests (cli.rs:561, 596, 631, 1040, 1107) write a locate cache under `~/.sufr`, keyed by basename only, never cleaned, staleness by mtime. Three share the key `locate-3-uniprot-masked.sufr`.

Duplicates and weak helpers:

- `extract_uniprot_masked_low_memory` (cli.rs:631) is identical to `extract_uniprot_masked` (cli.rs:596).
- The `summarize` helper (cli.rs:1137) skips a row whose regex does not match; two of twelve rows never match (sufr-f9b051).
- The count and locate helpers never compare stderr; extract does only when an error is expected.
- Expected output for the `.out` files and the inline extract strings came from running the binary (comments at cli.rs:430, 565, 600, 641, 922, 1086). The `.sufr` fixtures were committed by Ken in 2024 and the current code reproduces them byte for byte, which is the one independent check in the suite.

## Plan

Four batches, each a child issue.

1. An independent oracle for construction: a naive reference sort and reference LCP in the `libsufr` tests, run over every small `.fa` under the flag combinations, asserting the built array and LCP exactly. Replaces the vacuous sortedness tests.
2. Fixtures and the bytes test: every fixture read by a test or deleted, `mk_test_files.py` reproducing them, a decision on the 12 `create_*` tests.
3. Search: library tests with hand-derived expectations for the query kinds, mql cases, extract windows, locate order and the u64 width listed above.
4. Hardening: delete the vacuous and duplicate tests, a real empty-input test, the summarize helper failing on an unmatched row, the `-m` CLI tests run with `HOME` pointed at a temp dir.

## Open

- Batch 1 under `-m`: the reference LCP will disagree with the code (sufr-2b76b5). Pin the current values with a TODO, or fix first.
- Batch 3 on a later sequence: the extract window hits sufr-2fd179. Pin or fix first. Whether a query holding `$` matches the sentinel.
- Batch 2: keep one `create_*` test as the no-LCP write path, all twelve, or none.

notes.text: Jack decided on 2026-11-03 that this runs after the code changes already on the board, not before. A ranked list of the gaps that matter is being drawn up in conversation; the rows Jack picks from it become the scope, and the table in the body is the full inventory, not the plan.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: Rescoped on 2026-11-03 after Jack narrowed the CLAUDE.md rule to construction and search results. The body holds the scope. The sweep script and the memory benchmark-and-sweep-scripts were deleted the same day.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: Open item one decided on 2026-11-03: sufr-2b76b5 is fixed before batch 1 (sufr-a88738) so the reference LCP can be compared exactly on -m builds. The fix caps find_lcp's result and the N-run shortcut at max_query_len. No fixture is built with -m, so no fixture bytes move.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: Open item two decided on 2026-11-03: sufr-2fd179 is fixed before batch 3 (sufr-5cf0b7), with windows stopping at the last byte of the sequence. Queries holding the sentinel or delimiter keep matching for now; sufr-7b022c holds that decision and batch 3 pins the current behaviour.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: Open item three closed: the twelve create_* tests are deleted in c9c880d, see sufr-3d82d0.
